name: Hypertension
overview: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is persistently elevated arterial pressure, often silent until complications develop. It is a leading modifiable risk factor for stroke and heart disease in India. Regular screening and lifestyle plus medicines when needed greatly reduce long-term harm.
symptoms: Often no symptoms in early stages
Symptoms usually appear only after organ damage in untreated cases
causes: Primary (essential) hypertension — multifactorial in most adults
Secondary causes: renal disease, adrenal disorders, sleep apnoea, certain drugs
High sodium intake and low potassium diet
diagnosis: Repeated blood pressure measurements on separate visits
Home or ambulatory BP monitoring when white-coat effect suspected
Basic labs: kidney function, electrolytes, glucose, lipids
ECG and urine albumin for end-organ screening
treatment: Weight loss and DASH-style diet low in sodium
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, or diuretics as first-line options
Combination therapy often required for target BP
prevention: Limit salt to <5 g/day as per WHO guidance
Maintain healthy BMI and active lifestyle
Annual BP check after age 30, earlier if at risk
emergencySigns: BP ≥180/120 with chest pain or shortness of breath
Sudden weakness, speech difficulty, or facial droop (stroke)

faq.question: Can I rely on this Hypertension information instead of a doctor visit?
faq.answer: No. This content supports learning and preparation for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. It is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment.

faq.question: What should I do if Hypertension symptoms worsen suddenly?
faq.answer: Seek urgent medical care, especially if severe pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or high fever develops.
